title: Contributing to apa7
text: Fork package clone onto computer. haven’t done , recommend using usethis::create_from_github("wjschne/apa7", fork = TRUE). Install development dependencies devtools::install_dev_deps(), make sure package passes R CMD check running devtools::check(). R CMD check doesn’t pass cleanly, ’s good idea ask help continuing. Create Git branch pull request (PR). recommend using usethis::pr_init("brief-description--change"). Make changes, commit git, create PR running usethis::pr_push(), following prompts browser. title PR briefly describe change. body PR contain Fixes #issue-number. user-facing changes, add bullet top NEWS.md (.e. just first header). Follow style described https://style.tidyverse.org/news.html.

title: Contingency Tables
text: apa_chisq tests whether two variables independent, apa_note writes note: values , test effect size, many cases left missing values. text markdown, start “Note.” apaquarto adds . apaquarto, use apa_note apa-note chunk option. Chunk options evaluated chunk runs, make table earlier chunk (tbl_exercise made ): Table 2 Exercise Sex Note Exercise Female  Male  Total n % n % n % None  11   9.3   13  11.0   24  10.2  58  49.2   40  33.9   98  41.5 Frequent  49  41.5   65  55.1  114  48.3 Total 118 100.0  118 100.0  236 100.0 Without apaquarto, apa_flextable(note = TRUE) puts note table. combine apa-note chunk option, note appear twice. code: apa_note(tbl_exercise) [1] "Values are counts (*n*) and percentages of each column (each group of Sex). Chi-square test of independence: *χ*^2^(2, *N* = 236) = 5.72, *p* = .06, Cramér's *V* = .16. Cases with a missing value of Exercise or Sex (*n* = 1) are not included." ```{r} #| label: tbl-exercise-note #| apa7-width: landscape #| tbl-cap: "Exercise by Sex With a Note" #| apa-note: !expr apa7::apa_note(tbl_exercise) tbl_exercise ``` apa_flextable(tbl_exercise, note = TRUE) d_survey |>    filter_out(is.na(Sex)) |>    mutate(Exercise = fct_rev(Exercise)) |>    count(Sex, Exercise) |>    mutate(Proportion = n / sum(n), .by = Sex) |>    mutate(p = formatC(100 * Proportion, digits = 1, format = "f")) |>    ggplot(aes(Sex, Proportion)) +    geom_col(aes(fill = Exercise)) +    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(Exercise, ": ", p, "%"), group = Exercise), position = position_stack(vjust = .5, reverse = F), size = 16 * .8, size.unit = "pt", color = "white") +    scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion()) +   scale_y_continuous("Exercise Proportions", breaks = NULL, expand = expansion()) +    scale_fill_viridis_d(begin = .3, end = .7, direction = -1, alpha = .9) +   theme_minimal(base_family = "Open Sans", base_size = 16) +    theme(legend.position = "none", panel.grid = element_blank())

code: d_sat <- psych::sat.act |>   as_tibble() |>   mutate(     Gender = factor(gender, levels = 1:2, labels = c("Men", "Women")),     ACT,     `SAT-V` = SATV,     `SAT-Q` = SATQ   ) apa_htest(   d_sat,   ACT + `SAT-V` + `SAT-Q` ~ Gender ) |>    mutate(`*df*` = as.integer(`*df*`)) |>    apa_flextable() apa_htest(   d_sat,   ACT + `SAT-V` ~ Gender,   var_equal = TRUE,   effect_size = "hedges_g" ) tbl_greater <- apa_htest(   d_sat,   `SAT-Q` ~ Gender,   alternative = "greater" ) tbl_greater apa_note(tbl_greater) [1] "Welch's *t* test compares the groups of Gender without assuming equal variances. The *p*-value is one-sided (alternative: greater). Cohen's *d* uses the average of the two groups' variances. CI = confidence interval for Cohen's *d*."

title: Hypothesis Tests
text: sleep data, 10 patients took two sleep drugs. Paired data must wide format, one column per measurement. Put two variables pair Pair(), 1 right side formula, t.test: table note extracted apa_note says d standardized: Table 5 Paired-Samples t test Variable Drug 1  Drug 2 t(9) p dav 95% CI M SD M SD Drug 1 vs. Drug 2 0.75 1.79  2.33 2.00 −4.06 .003 −0.83 [−1.23, −0.43] one pair, variable names head descriptive statistics, differences first variable minus second. Paired data several versions Cohen’s d, differ standard deviation mean difference divided (Lakens, 2013): default, dav, scale d two independent groups, can compared -subjects studies. dz often much larger, SD differences small two variables highly correlated. describes consistent change rather large relative individual differences. "cohens_d" "d_av", "hedges_g" "g_av". come effectsize::repeated_measures_d. Table 6 Paired-Samples t Test dz Variable Drug 1  Drug 2 t(9) p dz 95% CI M SD M SD Drug 1 vs. Drug 2 0.75 1.79  2.33 2.00 −4.06 .003 −1.28 [−2.12, −0.45] Join several pairs + get one row per pair. descriptive statistics headed “First” “Second” unless set pair_labels. made-study, anxiety depression measured intervention: Table 7 Paired-Samples t Tests Anxiety Depression Treatment Variable Pretest  Posttest t(39) p dav 95% CI M SD M SD Anxiety Pre vs.    Anxiety Post 50.92 8.87  46.20  9.32  5.38 <.001  0.52 [ 0.33, 0.71] Depression Pre vs.    Depression Post 51.17 8.53  52.03 10.10 −0.95  .35  −0.09 [−0.28, 0.10] pair uses rows variables observed.

text: test = "wilcoxon", table shows group’s median (Mdn), Wilcoxon test statistic (W rank-sum test, V signed-rank test), rank-biserial correlation (rrb). Like correlations, rrb ranges −1 1 leading zero. Signed-rank tests use formulas one-sample paired t tests: Table 9 Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test Extra Sleep Two Drugs Variable Mdn V p rrb 95% CI Drug 1 Drug 2 Drug 1 vs. Drug 2 0.35 1.75 0 .009 −1.00 [−1.00, −1.00] Every patient slept Drug 2 (), rrb −1.00.

16) |>       ob_array(         k = 9,         sep = 0.35,         label = ob_label(           paste0(rep(c("V", "T", "S"), each = 3), "~", rep(1:3, 3), "~"),           color = "white",           fill abilities[rep(1:3, each = 3)],     tests,     resect = 2,     linewidth = .35,     label_sloped = FALSE,     label = ob_label(lbl(loadings$est.std),                       size = 13, model_pd <- " # Measurement model ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3 dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4 dem65 =~ y5 + y6 + y7 + y8 # Structural model dem60 ~ a * ind60 dem65 ~ c * ind60 + b * dem60 # Correlated residuals of matching indicators y1 ~~ y5 y2 ~~ y4 + y6 y3 ~~ y7 y4 ~~ y8 y6 ~~ y8 # Defined parameters indirect := a * b total := c + a * b " fit_pd <- sem(model_pd, data = PoliticalDemocracy) std_pd <- standardizedSolution(fit_pd) path <- function(lhs, rhs) { std_pd |> filter(op == "~", lhs == !!lhs, rhs == !!rhs) |> pull(est.std) |> lbl() } disturbance <- function(x) { std_pd |> filter(op == "~~", lhs == x, rhs == x) |> pull(est.std) |> lbl() } lb <- redefault( ob_label, nudge_y = -.1, fill = NA, color = "white", size = 14, lineheight = .95 ) lat <- redefault(ob_circle, radius = 1.5, color = NA) plb <- redefault(ob_label, size = 11, position = .47) ggdiagram(font_family = "Roboto Condensed", font_size = 16) + { ind60 <- lat( fill = my_fills[1], label = lb("Industrialization
1960")) } + { dem60 <- lat( fill = my_fills[2], label = lb("Democracy
1960") ) |> place(ind60, degree(30), sep = 2.5) } + { dem65 <- lat( fill = my_fills[3], label = lb( "Democracy
1965", nudge_y = -.1, fill = NA, color = "white", size = 15 ) ) |> place(dem60, degree(-30), sep = 2.5) } + connect( ind60, dem60, resect = 2, label_sloped = TRUE, label = plb( paste0("*a* = ", path("dem60", "ind60")), color = mean_color(c(ind60@fill, dem60@fill)) ) ) + connect( dem60, dem65, resect = 2, label_sloped = TRUE, label = plb( paste0("*b* = ", path("dem65", "dem60")), color = mean_color(c(dem60@fill, dem65@fill)) ) ) + connect( ind60, dem65, resect = 2, label_sloped = TRUE, label = plb( paste0("*c*′ = ", path("dem65", "ind60")), position = .5, color = mean_color(c(ind60@fill, dem65@fill)) ) ) + ob_variance( dem60, where = "north", resect = 2, looseness = 1.1, color = dem60@fill, label = ob_label( disturbance("dem60"), color = dem60@fill, size = 11) ) + ob_variance( dem65, where = "east", resect = 2, looseness = 1.1, color = dem65@fill, label = ob_label( disturbance("dem65"), color = dem65@fill, size = 11) ) apa_performance(fit_pd) tbl_pd <- apa_parameters(fit_pd, starred = "p") tbl_pd set.seed(2026) fit_pd_boot <- sem( model_pd, data = PoliticalDemocracy, se = "bootstrap", bootstrap = 500 ) apa_parameters( fit_pd_boot, standardize = FALSE, predictor_parameters = c("Parameter", "Coefficient", "SE", "CI", "Std_Coefficient") ) |> apa_flextable(note = TRUE)

Effect sizes computed data, depend function called, Cohen’s d Welch’s test exact rather approximated t. apa_note() says tests done, d standardized, abbreviations stand . apa_htest() runs paired t tests Wilcoxon signed-rank tests paired variables Pair() formula (e.g., apa_htest(d, Pair(pre, post) ~ 1), several pairs joined +).
